result.closed_gap: G043 recorded that AIR did not represent synchronization, side effects, memory-domain requirements or multi-device placement. Synchronization (AirBarrier over THREADGROUP/SIMDGROUP/DEVICE), side effects (writes_external on an op, read_only on an operand) and memory-domain requirements (7 named domains on every tensor plus an output domain) are now REPRESENTED. Placement was already a field.
result.the_discipline_that_makes_it_honest: REPRESENTING more than the backend can RUN is the point, but only if the two are never confused. lower_to_msl now calls executable_on_metal_backend() and REFUSES with the reason rather than emitting code that ignores the construct. A silently dropped barrier is a RACE -- the worst class of bug to ship quietly -- and a silently ignored memory domain would compute on the wrong copy.
result.vocabulary_shared_with_humf: AIR's memory domain names ARE HUMF's domain names, verified by a test that takes a requirement straight out of an AIR program and looks it up in a HUMF fabric with no mapping layer. A translation layer between them would be free to drift; there isn't one.

claim_boundary: AIR now REPRESENTS synchronization, side effects and memory domains. It EXECUTES none of them -- every such program is refused by the lowering, and the receipt above shows 4 of 5 probe cases refused. This widens the IR and narrows nothing about the backend. Multi-device placement remains a field with no backend that honours it, and there is still no GEMM, attention or reduction in AIR at all.
